records.source: אַל־תְּבַהֵ֨ל עַל־פִּ֜יךָ וְלִבְּךָ֧ אַל־יְמַהֵ֛ר לְהוֹצִ֥יא דָבָ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים בַּשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְאַתָּ֣ה עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ עַֽל־כֵּ֛ןיִהְי֥וּ דְבָרֶ֖יךָ מְעַטִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Do not be hasty with your mouth, and your heart, let it not hurry to bring out a word before God; for God [is] in the heavens and you [are] on the earth; therefore let your words be few.
pieces: Do not speak rashly, and do not let your heart be quick to say anything before God. God is in heaven and you are on earth, so keep your words few.

L.1: Do not be rash with your mouth, and let your heart not hurry to bring out a word before God, for God [is] in the heavens and you [are] on the earth; therefore let your words be few.

R.1: Think before you speak, and do not be quick to say anything to God. God is in heaven, and you are here on earth. So do not say too much.

decisions.choice: This verse is 5:1 in the Hebrew text, 5:2 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: Bibles that begin chapter 5 with the verse numbered 4:17 here (see the note there) number this chapter one higher: Hebrew 5:1-19 is their 5:2-20. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates, and cites the book by it.

decisions.choice: God in heaven, you on earth: the distance between God and people
decisions.reason: God is not one to bargain with or to address carelessly (Psalm 115:3, 16). The fitting response is reverence and few words, which verse 6 calls fearing God.

decisions.choice: bring out a word: speak, here in prayer or in making a vow
decisions.reason: Verses 3-5 show that the words in view include vows made before God.

decisions.choice: let your words be few: as Proverbs teaches
decisions.reason: "When words are many, wrongdoing is not lacking" (Proverbs 10:19; compare 17:28).

decisions.choice: Think before you speak
alternatives: Do not be rash with your mouth
decisions.reason: Readable says the same as the Hebrew idiom in a plain, positive form.

records.heading: Let your words be few

records.source: כִּ֛י בָּ֥א הַחֲל֖וֹם בְּרֹ֣ב עִנְיָ֑ן וְק֥וֹל כְּסִ֖יל בְּרֹ֥ב דְּבָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: For the dream comes with abundance of business, and the voice of a fool with abundance of words.
pieces: As dreams come when there is much to do, so a fool's voice comes with many words.

L.2: For the dream comes with much business, and the voice of a fool with many words.

R.2: People who are too busy have many dreams, and foolish people talk too much.

decisions.choice: a comparison: as busy-ness brings dreams, so the fool brings many words
decisions.reason: The two halves are set side by side in the way of a proverb: as a mind full of business produces dreams, so the fool produces words. Both are empty (verse 6).

decisions.choice: business: much to do, many cares
decisions.reason: The word ('inyan, see 1:13) is busy occupation.

decisions.choice: fool: kesil (see 2:14)
decisions.reason: The fool of Proverbs, who talks without thinking (Proverbs 10:14; 18:2).

decisions.choice: a fool's (B); foolish people (R)
decisions.reason: The book's wording for kesil, "fool" at Balanced and "foolish" at Readable.

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ תִּדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר לֵֽאלֹהִ֗ים אַל־תְּאַחֵר֙ לְשַׁלְּמ֔וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין חֵ֖פֶץ בַּכְּסִילִ֑ים אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־תִּדֹּ֖ר שַׁלֵּֽם׃
records.gloss: When you vow a vow to God, do not delay to pay it, for there is no pleasure in fools; what you vow, pay.
pieces: When you make a vow to God, do not put off paying it, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes no pleasure in fools. Pay what you vow.

L.3: When you vow a vow to God, do not delay to pay it, for [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] has no pleasure in fools. What you vow, pay.

R.3: If you make a promise to God, do not wait to keep it. God is not pleased with foolish people. Do what you promised.

decisions.choice: do not delay to pay a vow: the words of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The first words follow Deuteronomy 23:22: "When you vow a vow to the LORD your God, you shall not delay to pay it." Here the book says "God", as it always does, where Deuteronomy has the divine name.

decisions.choice: a vow: a promise made to God, often of an offering if God answered a prayer
decisions.reason: People vowed gifts or service to God, usually in a time of need (Genesis 28:20-22; 1 Samuel 1:11), and paid them at the sanctuary when the prayer was answered (Psalm 66:13-14).

decisions.choice: there is no pleasure in fools: God has none
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name who has no pleasure; the context shows it is God (compare Malachi 1:10).

decisions.choice: When you vow a vow ... do not delay to pay it (L); When you make a vow ... do not put off paying it (B); If you make a promise ... do not wait to keep it (R)
decisions.reason: Each level reuses its published wording of Deuteronomy 23:22, which this verse quotes (m1).

decisions.choice: [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the subject the Hebrew leaves understood (m3); Balanced supplies the pronoun and Readable names God.

decisions.choice: promise
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 23:22, Readable says "promise" for a vow.

records.gloss: Good that you not vow, more than that you vow and not pay.
pieces: It is better not to make a vow than to make one and not pay it.

L.4: Better that you do not vow than that you vow and do not pay.

R.4: It is better not to promise anything than to promise and not do it.

decisions.choice: better not to vow: as Deuteronomy allows
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 23:23 says that not vowing is no sin. A vow is free; breaking it is not.

records.source: אַל־תִּתֵּ֤ן אֶת־פִּ֨יךָ֙ לַחֲטִ֣יא אֶת־בְּשָׂרֶ֔ךָ וְאַל־תֹּאמַר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמַּלְאָ֔ךְ כִּ֥י שְׁגָגָ֖ה הִ֑יא לָ֣מָּה יִקְצֹ֤ף הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ עַל־קוֹלֶ֔ךָ וְחִבֵּ֖ל אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Do not give your mouth to cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before the messenger that it [was] a mistake; why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?
pieces: Do not let your mouth lead you into sin, and do not tell the messenger, "It was a mistake." Why should God be angry at what you say and destroy the work of your hands?

L.5: Do not let your mouth make your flesh sin, and do not say before the messenger that it [was] a mistake. Why should God be angry over your voice and ruin the work of your hands?

R.5: Do not let your words make you sin. And do not tell the temple messenger, "I did not mean that promise." Why should you make God angry by what you say? He might destroy everything you have worked for.

decisions.choice: the messenger: probably the priest or temple official who dealt with vows
decisions.reason: The word (mal'akh) means a messenger, human or divine. The priest is called "the messenger of the LORD of hosts" in Malachi 2:7, and vows were paid before priests at the sanctuary (Leviticus 27). The ancient Greek translation reads "before God" here. The text does not say more.

decisions.choice: a mistake: a sin done without meaning to
decisions.reason: The word (shegagah) is the term the law uses for sins done in error, for which there were offerings (Leviticus 4:2; Numbers 15:22-29). A careless vow cannot be excused as one.

decisions.choice: make your flesh sin: bring guilt on yourself
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for the whole person. Careless words lead the speaker into guilt.

decisions.choice: the temple messenger
decisions.reason: Readable says where the messenger would be met, in the reading taken (m1); it is marked uncertain with that decision.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for what you might say
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the excuse as direct speech, which English uses for this. Literal keeps the Hebrew "that".

records.source: כִּ֣י בְרֹ֤ב חֲלֹמוֹת֙ וַהֲבָלִ֔ים וּדְבָרִ֖ים הַרְבֵּ֑ה כִּ֥י אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְרָֽא׃
records.gloss: For in abundance of dreams and breaths and words many; but God, fear.
pieces: For when dreams and words are many, they are only a breath. Instead, fear God.

L.6: For in a multitude of dreams [there are] breaths, and many words; rather, fear God.

R.6: Dreaming a lot and talking a lot come to nothing, like a breath. Instead, honor God with awe.

decisions.choice: many dreams and many words are breath
alternatives: where there are many dreams there are many empty words
many dreams and empty words multiply
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets nouns side by side with no verb: "in many dreams and breaths and words many". The sense is clear enough: many dreams, like many words, come to nothing (verse 2). The exact grammar is not.

decisions.choice: breaths: empty things
decisions.reason: This is one of the few places where hevel is plural outside "breath of breaths" (1:2; 12:8). Here it means what is empty and comes to nothing.

decisions.choice: fear God: the right response to God, not many words
decisions.reason: Against careless words and vows, Qoheleth calls for the fear of God: reverent awe that takes God seriously (see the note at 3:14).

decisions.choice: honor God with awe
decisions.reason: The settled Readable wording for the fear of God (see 3:14). Literal and Balanced keep "fear God".

decisions.choice: only a breath (B); come to nothing, like a breath (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the breath picture and give its sense here (m2).

records.source: אִם־עֹ֣שֶׁק רָ֠שׁ וְגֵ֨זֶל מִשְׁפָּ֤ט וָצֶ֨דֶק֙ תִּרְאֶ֣ה בַמְּדִינָ֔ה אַל־תִּתְמַ֖הּ עַל־הַחֵ֑פֶץ כִּ֣י גָבֹ֜הַּ מֵעַ֤ל גָּבֹ֨הַ֙שֹׁמֵ֔ר וּגְבֹהִ֖ים עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: If oppression of a poor [one] and robbery of justice and righteousness you see in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for a high [one] over a high [one] is watching, and high [ones] over them.
pieces: If you see the poor oppressed in a province, and justice and right taken away by force, do not be surprised at it. One official watches over another, and still higher ones are over them both.

L.7: If you see the oppression of the poor and the robbing of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be amazed at the matter, for one high [official] watches over another high [official], and higher ones [are] over them.

R.7: In some places you may see poor people oppressed and treated unfairly by those in power. Do not be surprised. Each official has a higher official watching over them, and there are even higher officials over those.

decisions.choice: the province: a district ruled by officials for a distant king
decisions.reason: The word (medinah) is a district of an empire under a governor (2:8; Nehemiah 1:3; Esther 1:1).

decisions.choice: one high official watches over another, and higher ones over them: layers of officials
alternatives: each official watches out for himself and those above him, so the poor are squeezed at every level
decisions.reason: The word "high" (gavoah) is used three times, of officials one above another. "Watches" (shomer) can mean to keep watch over, to guard one's own interest, or to watch for a chance. Most take the line as a picture of officials protecting one another, so that injustice is built into the system and should cause no surprise. Others hear a hint that God, highest of all, sees what is done (3:17).

decisions.choice: robbing of justice and righteousness: justice taken away by force
decisions.reason: The word (gezel) is robbery by force (Ezekiel 18:18). Justice and right are stolen from the poor.

decisions.choice: [official]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "official", which the context gives to the adjective "high".

records.source: וְיִתְר֥וֹן אֶ֖רֶץ בַּכֹּ֣ל ה֑וּא מֶ֥לֶךְ לְשָׂדֶ֖ה נֶעֱבָֽד׃
records.gloss: And the advantage of a land in all it [is]: a king for a field [that is] tilled.
pieces: Yet, for all that, a land gains from having a king who cares for its farmed fields.

L.8: But the gain of a land in all [this] is: a king for a cultivated field.

R.8: But it is good for a country to have a king who cares about its farmland.

decisions.choice: a land gains from a king who looks after its farmland
alternatives: even a king is served by the field: everyone, up to the king, lives off the land
the gain from the land is taken by all, even by the king
decisions.reason: This is one of the hardest verses in the book. The Hebrew reads, word for word, "and the gain of a land in all it, a king for a field is served". It may mean that a king devoted to the land, who sees that fields are farmed, is a blessing; or that even the king depends on what the field produces, and so takes his share from the poor along with every official of verse 7. The Hebrew written text and its marginal reading differ by one small word here.

decisions.choice: gain: what is left over (see 1:3)
decisions.reason: The book's word yitron, here the advantage a land has.

decisions.choice: gains (B); it is good for (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the verb of "gain" and Readable says it plainly, as the book's wording for yitron allows (see 1:3).

records.source: אֹהֵ֥ב כֶּ֨סֶף֙ לֹא־יִשְׂבַּ֣ע כֶּ֔סֶף וּמִֽי־אֹהֵ֥ב בֶּהָמ֖וֹן לֹ֣א תְבוּאָ֑ה גַּם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃
records.gloss: [One] loving silver will not be satisfied [with] silver, and whoever loves abundance, not income; also this [is] breath.
pieces: Whoever loves money never has enough money, and whoever loves wealth is never satisfied with what comes in. This too is a breath.

L.9: Whoever loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, and whoever loves wealth [will not be satisfied with its] income. This too [is] breath.

R.9: People who love money will never have enough. People who love being rich will never be happy with what they earn. This too is like a breath; it cannot satisfy.

decisions.choice: silver: money
decisions.reason: Silver was weighed out as money before coins were used (Genesis 23:16), so the word (kesef) means both.

decisions.choice: wealth: abundance, riches
decisions.reason: The word (hamon) is a great quantity, here of possessions (Psalm 37:16).

decisions.choice: breath: it cannot satisfy
decisions.reason: Wealth never fills the desire for it; here hevel leans toward "empty" (see the note at 1:2).

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "silver" here (m1); Literal keeps "silver".

decisions.choice: [will not be satisfied with its]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words the second half borrows from the first.

records.source: בִּרְבוֹת֙ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה רַבּ֖וּ אוֹכְלֶ֑יהָ וּמַה־כִּשְׁרוֹן֙ לִבְעָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֖י אִם־רְא֥וּת עֵינָֽיו׃
records.gloss: In the increasing of the good, those eating it increase; and what success [is] to its owners except the sight of his eyes?
pieces: When good things increase, so do those who consume them. And what does their owner get from them, except to look at them?

L.10: When goods increase, those who eat them increase; and what profit [is there] for their owner except the sight of [them with] {{gender:their|his}} eyes?

R.10: The more a person owns, the more people come to use it up. The owner gets nothing from it except to look at it.

decisions.choice: goods: wealth, property
decisions.reason: The word (tovah, "good") means here good things, possessions.

decisions.choice: profit: benefit, success (see 2:21)
decisions.reason: The word (kishron) is not the book's "gain" (yitron) but means much the same here: what good it does.

decisions.choice: those who eat them: the household, servants and hangers-on who live off the wealth
decisions.reason: As wealth grows, so does the number of people it must feed, and the owner has nothing extra but the sight of it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The owner stands for any owner; the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default.

records.source: מְתוּקָה֙ שְׁנַ֣ת הָעֹבֵ֔ד אִם־מְעַ֥ט וְאִם־הַרְבֵּ֖ה יֹאכֵ֑ל וְהַשָּׂבָע֙ לֶֽעָשִׁ֔יר אֵינֶ֛נּוּ מַנִּ֥יחַֽ ל֖וֹ לִישֽׁוֹן׃
records.gloss: Sweet [is] the sleep of the worker, whether little or much he eats; and the plenty of the rich, it is not letting him sleep.
pieces: Workers sleep sweetly, whether they eat little or much, but the rich have so much that they cannot sleep.

L.11: Sweet [is] the sleep of the laborer, whether {{gender:they eat|he eats}} little or much; but the plenty of the rich does not let {{gender:them|him}} sleep.

R.11: People who work hard sleep well, whether they have a little or a lot to eat. But rich people have so much that they lie awake at night.

decisions.choice: the laborer: one who works for a living, especially on the land
decisions.reason: The word ('oved) is a worker, often one who works the ground (Genesis 4:2).

decisions.choice: plenty: abundance, a full stomach or many possessions
decisions.reason: The word (sava') is fullness or plenty. It may mean the rich man's full stomach or his many goods and the worries they bring; either way it keeps him awake.

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: people ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of any person with a masculine singular. Balanced and Readable speak of people in general, which needs no setting; Literal keeps the singular with the gender setting.

records.source: יֵ֚שׁ רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עֹ֛שֶׁר שָׁמ֥וּר לִבְעָלָ֖יו לְרָעָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: There is a sickening evil [which] I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owners to his harm.
pieces: I have seen a painful misfortune under the sun: wealth hoarded by its owner to the owner's own harm.

L.12: There is a sickening evil [that] I have seen under the sun: wealth guarded by its owner to {{gender:their|his}} harm.

R.12: I have seen something very sad here on earth. People save up wealth, and it hurts them.

decisions.choice: a sickening evil: a misfortune that is painful to see
decisions.reason: The words (ra'ah cholah) mean a sickly or grievous evil. It is not wickedness but a misfortune (5:15; 6:1-2).

decisions.choice: wealth kept to his harm: hoarded wealth that turns against its owner
decisions.reason: The next verse tells how: the wealth is lost, and nothing is left.

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: a painful misfortune (B); something very sad (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of ra'ah here (m1); in modern English "evil" would suggest wickedness.

records.source: וְאָבַ֛ד הָעֹ֥שֶׁר הַה֖וּא בְּעִנְיַ֣ן רָ֑ע וְהוֹלִ֣יד בֵּ֔ן וְאֵ֥ין בְּיָד֖וֹ מְאֽוּמָה׃
records.gloss: And that wealth was lost in an evil business, and he fathered a son, and there [was] nothing in his hand.
pieces: Then that wealth is lost through some bad venture, and when he has a son, he has nothing left to give him.

L.13: And that wealth was lost in an evil venture, and he fathered a son, and there [was] nothing in his hand.

R.13: Then he loses it all through some bad business. He has a son, but he has nothing to give him.

decisions.choice: an evil venture: a bad business deal, a misfortune
decisions.reason: The words ('inyan ra') are the ones used in 1:13 and 4:8. Here they mean an undertaking that goes wrong.

decisions.choice: nothing in his hand: nothing for the son to inherit
alternatives: the father himself has nothing left
decisions.reason: "His hand" may be the son's, who inherits nothing, or the father's, who has nothing to give. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: he ... a son
decisions.reason: The case is told of a particular father, so no inclusive wording is used.

decisions.choice: to give him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain what the empty hand means (m2).

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר יָצָא֙ מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמּ֔וֹ עָר֛וֹם יָשׁ֥וּב לָלֶ֖כֶת כְּשֶׁבָּ֑א וּמְא֨וּמָה֙ לֹא־יִשָּׂ֣א בַעֲמָל֔וֹ שֶׁיֹּלֵ֖ךְ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: As he came out from the womb of his mother, naked he will return, to go as he came; and anything he will not carry in his toil which he may take in his hand.
pieces: As he came from his mother's womb, so he must go back, naked as he came. He will take nothing from all his hard work that he can carry in his hand.

L.14: As he came out of his mother's womb, naked he will return, going as he came; and he will carry nothing from his toil that he may take in his hand.

R.14: He came from his mother's body with nothing, and he will leave this world with nothing. He cannot take with him anything he worked for.

decisions.choice: naked from the womb, naked to return: as Job said
decisions.reason: Job said, "Naked I came out of my mother's womb, and naked I will return there" (Job 1:21). Death takes away all that toil has gathered.

decisions.choice: he: the man of verse 13, and anyone like him
decisions.reason: The words continue the case of verses 12-13, but what they say holds for everyone (verse 15).

decisions.choice: he will leave this world with nothing
decisions.reason: Readable says what "naked" and "return" mean here; Literal and Balanced keep the words of Job 1:21.

records.source: וְגַם־זֹה֙ רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה כָּל־עֻמַּ֥ת שֶׁבָּ֖א כֵּ֣ן יֵלֵ֑ךְ וּמַה־יִּתְר֣וֹן ל֔וֹ שֶֽׁיַּעֲמֹ֖ל לָרֽוּחַ׃
records.gloss: And also this [is] a sickening evil: exactly as he came, so he will go; and what advantage [is] to him that he toils for the wind?
pieces: This too is a painful misfortune: just as he came, so he must go. And what does he gain from toiling for the wind?

L.15: And this too [is] a sickening evil: exactly as he came, so he will go; and what gain [is there] for him who toils for the wind?

R.15: This too is very sad. People leave this world the same way they came into it. So what good does it do them to work so hard for wind?

decisions.choice: toils for the wind: works for what cannot be held
decisions.reason: Wind cannot be kept (1:14; Proverbs 11:29 "inherits the wind"). Toil for wealth that must be left behind is toil for wind.

decisions.choice: gain: the question of 1:3 again
decisions.reason: The book's word yitron: nothing is left over when a person dies.

decisions.choice: a painful misfortune (B); very sad (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

decisions.choice: People ... them
decisions.reason: Readable says "people" to make plain that what was said of one man holds for all (verse 14, m2).

records.source: גַּ֥ם כָּל־יָמָ֖יו בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ יֹאכֵ֑ל וְכָעַ֥ס הַרְבֵּ֖ה וְחָלְי֥וֹ וָקָֽצֶף׃
records.gloss: Also all his days in darkness he eats, and he is vexed much, and his sickness and anger.
pieces: All his days he eats in darkness, with much vexation, sickness and anger.

L.16: Also all his days he eats in darkness, and [he is] greatly vexed, and [has] sickness and anger.

R.16: All his life he eats his meals in gloom. He is very upset, sick and angry.

decisions.choice: eats in darkness: lives in gloom
decisions.reason: To eat in darkness is to spend one's days without joy, the opposite of eating with joy (9:7).

decisions.choice: vexed ... sickness and anger: a list without verbs
alternatives: his days are spent in darkness and mourning (reading slightly different letters)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew piles up nouns at the end of the sentence. Some read slightly different letters and get "in darkness and mourning". The general sense is clear: the life of the hoarder is full of frustration, illness and anger.

decisions.choice: [he is] ... [has]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the verbs English needs (m2).

records.source: הִנֵּ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־רָאִ֣יתִי אָ֗נִי ט֣וֹב אֲשֶׁר־יָפֶ֣ה לֶֽאֶכוֹל־וְ֠לִשְׁתּוֹת וְלִרְא֨וֹת טוֹבָ֜ה בְּכָל־עֲמָל֣וֹ׀שֶׁיַּעֲמֹ֣ל תַּֽחַת־הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ מִסְפַּ֧ר יְמֵי־חַיָּ֛יואֲשֶׁר־נָֽתַן־ל֥וֹ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־ה֥וּא חֶלְקֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Look, what I have seen, I: good, which [is] fitting, [is] to eat and to drink and to see good in all his toil which he toils under the sun the number of the days of his life which God has given to him, for it [is] his portion.
pieces: This is what I have seen to be good and fitting: for people to eat and drink and enjoy all their hard work under the sun during the few days of life God has given them, for that is their share.

L.17: Look, what I have seen [to be] good, what [is] fitting: to eat and to drink and to see good in all {{gender:their|his}} toil at which {{gender:they toil|he toils}} under the sun [for] the number of the days of {{gender:their|his}} life that God has given {{gender:them|him}}, for that [is] {{gender:their|his}} portion.

R.17: This is what I have learned is good and right: people should eat and drink and enjoy their hard work here on earth during the short life God has given them. That is what life gives them.

decisions.choice: good and fitting: what is good and right for the time
decisions.reason: The word "fitting" (yafeh) is the one used in 3:11: what is right in its time.

decisions.choice: the portion God gives: life to enjoy now
decisions.reason: As in 2:24, 3:13 and 3:22, eating, drinking and enjoying work is the share God gives for the few days of life. After the hoarder of verses 12-16, Qoheleth sets out what is good.

decisions.choice: the number of the days of his life: the short, counted days (see 2:3)
decisions.reason: Days that can be counted are few.

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: share (B); what life gives them (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for cheleq (see 2:10).

decisions.choice: the few days of life (B); the short life (R)
alternatives: the number of the days of his life
decisions.reason: As in 2:3.

records.source: גַּ֣ם כָּֽל־הָאָדָ֡ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן־ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֩ עֹ֨שֶׁר וּנְכָסִ֜ים וְהִשְׁלִיט֨וֹ לֶאֱכֹ֤ל מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ וְלָשֵׂ֣את אֶת־חֶלְק֔וֹ וְלִשְׂמֹ֖חַ בַּעֲמָל֑וֹ זֹ֕ה מַתַּ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃
records.gloss: Also every man to whom God has given wealth and riches and has given him power to eat from it and to take up his portion and to rejoice in his toil, this [is] a gift of God.
pieces: And whenever God grants people riches and property, and lets them eat from it, take up their share and be glad in their hard work, that is God's gift.

L.18: Also every {{gender:person|man}} to whom God has given wealth and possessions, and has given {{gender:them|him}} power to eat from them and to take up {{gender:their|his}} portion and to rejoice in {{gender:their|his}} toil—this [is] a gift of God.

R.18: If God gives people wealth and lets them enjoy it, accept what life gives them and be happy in their work, that is a gift from God.

decisions.choice: given him power: enabled him, allowed him
decisions.reason: The verb (shalat, see 2:19) means to have power over, here to be able to use and enjoy. God gives not only wealth but the ability to enjoy it; 6:2 tells of one who has the wealth without that power.

decisions.choice: a gift of God: as in 3:13
decisions.reason: The words repeat 3:13: enjoyment is given, not earned.

decisions.choice: portion: the share given (see 2:10)
decisions.reason: To take up one's portion is to accept and enjoy the share God gives.

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: share (B); what life gives them (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for cheleq (see 2:10).

records.source: כִּ֚י לֹ֣א הַרְבֵּ֔ה יִזְכֹּ֖ר אֶת־יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֑יו כִּ֧י הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים מַעֲנֶ֖ה בְּשִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For not much will he remember the days of his life, for God [is] occupying [him] with the joy of his heart.
pieces: Such people will not dwell much on the days of their lives, because God keeps them busy with gladness of heart.

L.19: For {{gender:they|he}} will not much remember the days of {{gender:their|his}} life, because God keeps {{gender:them|him}} occupied with the joy of {{gender:their|his}} heart.

R.19: They will not spend much time worrying about how short life is, because God keeps them busy enjoying life.

decisions.choice: keeps him occupied: keeps him busy with joy
alternatives: answers him with joy: God responds by giving joy
decisions.reason: The verb (ma'aneh) can come from the root of "to be busy" ('anah, as in the word for "task", 1:13) or from the root "to answer". Either God keeps the person busy with joy, or God answers him with it. The first follows the book's use of the root.

decisions.choice: not much remember the days of his life: not brood over how short and hard life is
decisions.reason: A person busy with God-given joy does not dwell on the brevity and troubles of life (2:23; 6:12).

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: spend much time worrying about how short life is
alternatives: remember the days of their life much
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m2).
